Thanks. So with the node environment, you variable is not being created in the global scope. Node has its own scope just under the global scope, so top-level variable and functions end up in that score instead of global.

Oh, hmmm...for some reason I misread your config file as having `node: true`. Disregard my earlier comment and sorry for the confusion.

This does appear to be a bug.

I've tried `var formatters = {}` both with `no-unused-vars` configured with just `locals` and defining `formatters` explicitly with `globals` and have been unable to reproduce the problem.

Do you have any other `.eslintrc` files in the project? Our configurations cascade, so they get combined.

Can you share what other code is in the file?

Thanks, that's very helpful. As best I can tell from my quick debugging, `formatters` is being added to a function scope instead of the global scope. It looks like `ecmaFeatures.globalReturn` is somehow being toggled to `true`. Still unsure how that's happening, but investigating.
Found it. Looks like we're not checking `true` or `false`, just the presence of the key. Easy fix.

note: `jscheck` was the original project name before I found out it was taken. :) Just never changed my directory.

I just figured out I was still running 0.16.1. grunt-eslint has a dependency on eslint "^0.16.1", which I had tried overriding to "0.16.2" in a few different ways, but apparently none of them worked. I ended up just manually copying the eslint 0.16.2 files over top of node_modules/grunt-eslint/node_modules/eslint/, in order to try running 0.16.2 on my project via grunt (where we specify which js files to include, etc.). Once I did this, the invalid warnings disappeared.

I'm still not sure why 0.16.2 wasn't getting pulled down and used automatically, since I'm pretty sure "^0.16.1" should match any 0.16.x version >= 0.16.1. It could be something to do with the local npm lazy mirror that my team uses not working as I expected.

 Sorry for the false alarm, and thanks again!
No problem, I actually was wondering if maybe you were using ESLint through an intermediary. In any event, glad it got fixed.
@nzakas I was going to name my project jscop before I saw that eslint used exactly the same approach:-)
